references.text: Moses gives the same command to Joshua to be strong and courageous, assuring him that the Lord will go before him.
Moses speaks directly to Joshua and exhorts him to be strong and courageous, with the promise of the Lord's presence.
The Lord Himself commands Joshua to be strong and courageous, with the promise to be with him.
The same exhortation to Joshua to be strong and very courageous, linked to obedience to God's law.
God's promise to be with His people and strengthen them, with an encouragement not to fear.
The Lord's promise to be with His people through all trials.
God's assurance of His presence: 'Do not fear, for I am with you.'
The Lord's promise to Jeremiah to be with him and deliver him.
The author quotes God's promise never to leave or forsake believers as the basis for boldness.
Jesus' promise to be with His disciples all days until the end of the age.
Paul's assurance that if God is for us, no one can stand against us.
